messages:
jonah (customer): Hey team, after our corporate IdP SSO redirect users get logged in but immediately hit MFA again — effectively infinite re-prompt. Happening for a subset of users on Chrome 118 on macOS.
maria (support): Thanks for the report. Sorry you're hitting this. Quick q: is the app embedded in an iframe or used as a top-level redirect? Also can you paste the Set-Cookie headers from the IdP / token exchange response?
jonah (customer): It's a top-level redirect flow (OIDC). I captured the redirect trace:

```
GET /auth/callback?code=abc123 302 -> Location: https://app.example.com/sso/complete
-> GET /sso/complete 200 Set-Cookie: session=; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=0
```

Users land on the app but session is blank and auth tries to re-initiate. This started after our IdP rotated signing keys last week.
ellie (auth): @maria @jonah that Set-Cookie looks suspicious — Max-Age=0 means cookie expires immediately. Did the IdP upstream start sending that? Also SameSite=Strict can break some cross-site flows but since you said top-level redirect it shouldn't. We need the full response headers from the token exchange (POST /oauth/token) and the app's set-cookie logic.
maria (support): @jonah can you run this quick curl repro and paste output? `curl -i -L -s "https://idp.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code"` then follow the final exchange `curl -i -X POST https://idp.example.com/oauth/token -d 'code=abc123&grant_type=authorization_code&redirect_uri=...'`
jonah (customer): Pasting the token exchange response headers:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: device_trust=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=2592000
Set-Cookie: session=; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=0
Content-Type: application/json
```

So device_trust cookie is set fine, session is being cleared.
kevin (eng-oncall): Echoing @ellie: Max-Age=0 is the problem. Two quick hypotheses:
  1) The app code is intentionally clearing session when it sees an old cookie or mismatch (e.g., mismatch between device_trust and session user id) — maybe due to signature change after IdP key rotation.
  2) Our cookie-setting layer is hitting a value length or attr validation bug that defaults Max-Age to 0 on failure.

Can you paste the backend log around the token exchange (trace id)? We can search for cookie-write errors.
maria (support): Also adding checklist: browser devtools network capture, curl headers (done), backend logs, any 403/401 from our session store, and whether this happens for users with existing active sessions or only new sign-ins.
jonah (customer): Logs from our app show:

```
2026-02-20T14:12:04Z auth: INFO exchange success for sub=joe@example.com trace=tr-0912
2026-02-20T14:12:04Z session: WARN cookie write failed: invalid-expires-format, falling back to zero
```

That invalid-expires-format error looks new after IdP rotation.
ellie (auth): That makes sense — if the IdP started returning expires_at in a format we parse into cookie expiry and the parser fails, our cookie util might set Max-Age=0 as a safe default. We recently merged a change that accepts RFC3339 or UNIX secs, but maybe the IdP returned RFC1123. Can you paste the token JSON body (with any sensitive tokens redacted)?
jonah (customer): Token body (redacted):

```
{
  "access_token": "[redacted]",
  "expires_at": "Sat, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:04 GMT",
  "id_token": "[redacted]"
}
```

We do return expires_at in RFC1123.
kevin (eng-oncall): Okay this is actionable. Our cookie util expects ISO8601 or epoch seconds. If expires_at is RFC1123, parse fails -> invalid-expires-format -> Max-Age=0. Short-term workaround: set COOKIE_FALLBACK_TTL env to 30d so we force non-zero expiry when parse fails. Long term: update parser to accept RFC1123 and fallback heuristics.
maria (support): For @jonah: can you set COOKIE_FALLBACK_TTL=2592000 in your deployment and redeploy your auth service? That should unblock users until we ship the parser patch.
jonah (customer): Deploying now, I'll report back in 5.
session-bot: deploy started by jonah (customer) — commit 4f9a2b — rolling update to auth-service

(5m later)
jonah (customer): Deployed and verified. No more immediate MFA loop for previously affected users. Thanks!
maria (support): Great. Next steps:
- engineering (ellie/kevin) to ship parser patch to accept RFC1123 and add unit tests (ETA: 48h)
- support to monitor for related tickets and update KB with workaround env var
- customer to confirm if any users still hit issue after 24h

ellie (auth): I'll open a PR today and include a migration test against sample IdP payloads. Will tag @kevin for code review.
kevin (eng-oncall): I'll also check cookie-util library for other silent fallbacks and audit downstream services.
maria (support): Closing the high-severity customer impact once parser patch merges and we validate. Marking this thread with follow-up tasks and informing account manager. :white_check_mark:
jonah (customer): Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
